title: Latency signal mosaic: route/model streaming-flag comparator and drift alerts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a new observability dashboard and alerting surface that compares latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) across model + route groupings while explicitly overlaying the streaming vs non-streaming request flag. This is intended to make regressions that are driven by streaming heuristics, batching changes, or KV cache behavior visible to SREs and product owners, and to provide automated drift detection that can open incidents or trigger rollbacks.
background: We have multiple teams asking why p95 spikes on a route but only for streaming requests, or why model A shows tail degradation after a runtime change. Existing boards surface percentiles by model/route but naming conventions and streaming flag hooks are inconsistent. Traces do not always link back to panels with streaming/non-streaming context which makes root cause slow.
proposal:
1) Enrich tracing hooks and request telemetry with a canonical boolean 'io_mode' tag: 'streaming'|'blocking'. Ensure SDKs and gateways set this for all requests.
2) Update the metrics pipeline to emit separate percentile series for streaming and blocking variants per (model, route) key using the existing telemetry aggregation layer.
3) Create a "Latency Signal Mosaic" dashboard that:
   - Shows p50/p95/p99 sparklines for model+route rows with small inline bars for streaming vs blocking split.
   - Provides a drift heatmap where each cell is % change in p95 vs 7d baseline, color-coded and clickable to open trace links.
   - Adds an interactive selector to focus on single model across routes or single route across models.
   - Includes a synthetic workload panel to replay representative requests for the selected cohort and compare baseline vs current quantiles.
4) Add alerting rules: p95(current 5m) > 1.25 * p95(7d baseline) AND p99 delta > 30ms for any (model,route,io_mode) with >1000 requests/day. Alerts create PagerDuty incidents and annotate the dashboard with the incident id.
5) Instrument a small set of canary routes with extra KV cache miss counters to correlate cache effects with tail latency.
implementation_plan:
- Week 1: Schema design and trace hook changes (telemetry proto). Update edge SDKs and gateway to set io_mode flag. -> PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-sdk/pull/1820
- Week 2: Metrics pipeline: add separate aggregation keys and pipelines for streaming/blocking percentiles. Work with infra to ensure cardinality controls.
- Week 3: Dashboard wireframe and quick mock in console. Iterate with PM/Product-UX. -> doc: drive.redwood.ai/LatencySignalMosaic/design-v1
- Week 4: Build viz panels, link trace explorer, add synthetic playback harness.
- Week 5: Add alerts & runbook, smoke test on staging, onboard 2 customer routes as canaries.
- Week 6: Rollout to prod and run 2-week observational window, collect feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hook 'io_mode' present on 100% of production requests and backfilled for 7d via logs where possible
Metrics pipeline emits distinct p50/p95/p99 series for streaming/blocking for all active model/route keys
Dashboard exists in Console with filtering by model/route and streaming overlay; sparklines render within <500ms for up to 200 rows
Alerting rule fires on synthesized regressions in staging and creates incidents with links to the dashboard and sample traces
Correlation panel shows KV cache miss rate aligned with p99 spikes for at least one canary route
tasks: Define telemetry schema and proto changes
Update edge SDKs/gateway to set io_mode
Extend aggregation layer to maintain streaming/blocking percentile series
Build dashboard panels and heatmap UX
Instrument synthetic workload runner for cohort playback
Add Prometheus/Alertmanager rules or equivalent in metric-alerting system
Create runbook and link to PagerDuty escalation policy
Smoke test and run canary for 2 routes
notes: Cardinality is a concern: we will only emit separate streaming/blocking series for model+route combos that exceed a minimal traffic threshold (configurable, default 100 req/day) to keep storage costs down. If storage/ingest limits are hit, we'll fall back to computing streaming/blocking deltas via daily batch jobs and show approximate deltas in the dashboard.
